test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: general
question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 24 minutes, respectively, while a third pipe C can empty the full tank in 32 minutes. All the three pipes are opened simultaneously. However, pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled. In how much time (in minutes) will the tank be full?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity (LCM of 12, 24, 32) = 96 units.

Efficiencies: A = 8, B = 4, C = −3 (emptying).

Net efficiency (A + B − C) = 8 + 4 − 3 = 9 units/min.

Work not emptied by C in the last 2 minutes = 3 × 2 = 6 units.

Time taken to fill = (96 − 6) ÷ 9 = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 12 minutes

Time taken by Pipe B = 24 minutes

Time taken by Pipe C (emptying) = 32 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

Let the total time to fill the tank be T minutes.

Pipe A and B work for the entire duration T.

Pipe C is closed 2 minutes before filling, so Pipe C works for (T − 2) minutes.

⇒ Work done by A + Work done by B − Work emptied by C = Total capacity

⇒ (8 × T) + (4 × T) − 3 × (T − 2) = 96

⇒ 12T − 3T + 6 = 96

⇒ 9T + 6 = 96

⇒ 9T = 90

⇒ T = 10 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 10 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

Filling pipes have positive efficiency, while emptying pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency. Net efficiency is the algebraic sum of all active pipe efficiencies.

Closing Pipes Early

If a pipe is closed x minutes before completion, assume it works for (T − x) minutes, where T is the total time.

Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the task alone, given constant total work (Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time).

**∴ The correct answer is 10 minutes.**</p
